title: Lior and the Vow
premise: Marguerite Yarrow's struggling café survives on one thing: the winter lantern festival's pastry contract, which she lost five years ago to her culinary-school rival, Julian Voss. When a snowstorm strands them both in a mountain inn with the unfinished confession from the night that ended their partnership, they are forced to confront the choice Julian made to save his own career — the choice that cost Marguerite everything. Over three snowbound days and one festival deadline, old love and old betrayal collide, and Marguerite must decide whether winning means taking back the contract or trusting the man who broke her. In the end she wins the festival on her own terms, and Julian, choosing her over the career that once saved him, asks to start again not as rivals but as partners.
about_author: Rafael Underhill is a former line cook who traded kitchen heat for the quiet of a coastal writing cabin, where he writes love stories seasoned with flour, salt, and regret. He believes the best romances, like the best bread, require patience, heat, and a willingness to be changed.

chapters.title: Three Payments from Gone
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A bank letter and a broken oven open the chapter as Marguerite counts her café's remaining days. Her assistant Bea urges her to re-enter the lantern festival competition she swore off five years ago. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into stubborn pride.

chapters.title: The Name on the Letterhead
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The festival contract she needs is now awarded through Julian Voss's restaurant group — her old partner turned empire-builder. She drafts an angry application, then a careful one, and sends both by accident. Emotional beat: humiliation braided with defiance.

chapters.title: Julian, Five Years On
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian reads Marguerite's application in his glass office and feels the past arrive like weather. His business partner warns him against entanglement; he approves her entry anyway. Emotional beat: success revealed as a gilded kind of emptiness.

chapters.title: The Road to Ashford Inn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both are summoned to a judges' retreat at a mountain inn. Marguerite's bus and Julian's car converge on the same snowed-in road; the storm closes it behind them. Emotional beat: dread and a traitorous flutter of anticipation.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The inn's generator fails, the judges cancel, and Marguerite realizes she is trapped for days with Julian Voss. Their first conversation is barbed, professional, and too careful. Emotional beat: the past pressing against a locked door.

chapters.title: What the Kitchen Remembers
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Snowbound, they cook together from instinct — his hands remembering hers, her orders arriving before he asks. A shared plate at midnight tastes like their twenties. Emotional beat: muscle memory as confession.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Wine, candlelight, and the inn's silence lower her guard. They nearly kiss; she pulls back and demands the truth about the night she lost everything. He begins to answer. Emotional beat: longing colliding with old wounds.

chapters.title: The Night He Chose
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confesses: their mentor offered one partnership slot, and he took it without telling her, believing he was saving them both from ruin. She was meant to be thanked, not betrayed — that's how he told it to himself. Emotional beat: guilt finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Five Years of Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She tells her side — the shame, the rebuilding, the café as a fortress built one careful brick at a time. She accuses him of choosing ambition over her; he cannot fully deny it. Emotional beat: grief given its proper weight.

chapters.title: A Truce in Flour
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Neither can sleep; they bake bread for the stranded inn staff as penance and peace treaty. Laughter returns, tentative and startling. Emotional beat: the first warmth neither of them names.

chapters.title: Bea's Phone Call
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Bea calls: the café's landlord is threatening eviction, and the festival prize is now the only rescue. Marguerite realizes the competition isn't a choice anymore — and Julian overhears. Emotional beat: stakes made brutally personal.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian offers to withdraw his own entry and fund her café, no strings. Marguerite refuses — she won't be charity, or a debt, or his penance. Emotional beat: pride as both armor and cage.

chapters.title: Snowmelt
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The storm breaks; the roads open. On the inn's porch they almost say what they mean, and instead agree to meet at the festival as competitors. The drive home is silent. Emotional beat: tenderness deferred until it aches.

chapters.title: The Café at Dawn
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Back home, Marguerite bakes her festival entry — a pastry built from their shared past, then remade into something entirely hers. Bea sees the truth on her face and says nothing. Emotional beat: turning memory into material.

chapters.title: Julian's Empty Kitchen
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian tests his competition entry and finds it flawless and hollow. His partner pushes him to crush Marguerite publicly; Julian hesitates, and the hesitation costs him his partner's trust. Emotional beat: ambition losing its flavor.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Rumor
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A leak suggests Marguerite's entry plagiarizes Julian's old recipes; festival organizers demand proof of originality. She suspects his partner, but doubt poisons everything Julian told her. Emotional beat: the past weaponized against hope.

chapters.title: The Confrontation
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marguerite confronts Julian the night before the festival; he denies involvement but cannot prove it, and she walks away. Alone, Julian finds the leak's source — his own partner — and makes his choice. Emotional beat: betrayal repeated, then refused.

chapters.title: What Julian Gives Up
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian exposes the sabotage at the cost of his partnership, his name on the contract, and his reputation's polish. He tells Marguerite only afterward, expecting nothing. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in reverse.

chapters.title: Festival Night
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Under the lanterns, Marguerite presents her pastry — honest, original, hers — before the judges and the town. She wins the contract on merit, and the café is saved by her own hands. Emotional beat: triumph that feels incomplete without him.

chapters.title: The Question Under the Lanterns
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian finds her after the judging, stripped of title and empire, and asks for nothing but the chance to begin as equals. Marguerite makes him wait — one full breath, one full year of memory. Then she takes his hand. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Yarrow and Voss
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Weeks later, the café's sign gains a second name; two ovens, two stations, one kitchen. They negotiate like rivals and move around each other like partners. Emotional beat: belonging built rather than found.

chapters.title: The Vow
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On the first snow of the next winter, Julian proposes not with a ring but with a written vow — the choice he failed to make at twenty-five, made plain at last. She answers with a pastry and a yes. Emotional beat: the price of survival finally worth paying.
